title: Atlas of cell types and regulatory elements underlying human facial diversity.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC: paywalled, no PMCID, no supplement, no text-mined accessions. NCBI elink from PubMed 42786296 returns only PubMed-to-PubMed links (no GEO/SRA/BioProject). GEO searches (author Adameyko, Erickson A + face, craniofacial multiome, facial spatial embryo) found no matching series. CELLxGENE (397 collections scanned) has no collection for this paper; the facial collection found belongs to a different Cotney-lab paper. BioStudies/ArrayExpress search found nothing. Zenodo DOI search returned 0 hits; a title search found one companion record (17347142, CC-BY-4.0) holding only microCT scans: 3 human embryo DICOM zips of 2.2-3.9 GB and 6 STL meshes plus one 676 MB mouse zip. Listing read from the Zenodo API, files not downloaded.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the single-cell RNA, chromatin accessibility (ATAC) and spatial transcriptomics data (embryonic weeks 6-11, 56 cell states, enhancer-gene links) comes from the abstract only. Where these data are deposited, and whether access is controlled (likely for human embryonic tissue, e.g. EGA, the European Genome-phenome Archive), could not be determined without the paywalled data availability statement.

a1_downloadable.note: No open deposit of the single-cell or chromatin data found in GEO, SRA, CELLxGENE, BioStudies or Zenodo via repository metadata. The only open deposit is microCT imaging of 3 embryos. Human embryonic sequencing data may be in a controlled-access archive such as EGA, but this is unconfirmed.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked in files (none found). Any task, such as predicting cell-type chromatin accessibility of an enhancer from its DNA sequence, would need a peak-by-cell-type matrix built from processed data whose existence is unverified.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not verifiable: no processed files located.

a4_units_stated.note: Not verifiable: no processed files located.

a6_fits_laptop.note: No processed matrix located to size.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessable without data. Cell-state labels in atlases come from clustering, which is a computed annotation, not a measurement.

backbone.name: AlphaGenome or Nucleotide Transformer (DNA language models) for enhancer sequences, if the chromatin data were obtainable
backbone.hardware: CPU for embedding a few tens of thousands of peaks; not tested

integration.partner_dataset: Facial-shape GWAS summary statistics (White et al. 2021, Nature Genetics, 203 signals)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do sequence models trained on cell-type-resolved facial enhancers explain which facial-shape GWAS variants act in which mesenchymal cell state?

controls.external_validation: Possible: Cotney-lab human craniofacial snRNA-seq on CELLxGENE (collection 690fb28b) and the 2024 craniofacial enhancer atlas, if this atlas's data were obtainable.

honest_claim_h3: No claim possible: the processed single-cell and chromatin data for this atlas could not be located in any open repository.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA sequence of facial enhancers to predict in which embryonic facial cell types each enhancer is open and active.
plain_idea.train_on: DNA sequences of regulatory regions (enhancers) mapped in the atlas; number unknown because the chromatin data could not be found.
plain_idea.predict: Whether each region is accessible (open chromatin, measured by single-cell ATAC sequencing) in each of the atlas's cell states.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Craniofacial geneticists could score facial-shape and cleft-risk variants for which embryonic cell type they disrupt, prioritising mouse enhancer experiments like the paper's PAX1 test.

ml_idea: Cell-type-resolved enhancer accessibility prediction from sequence with a frozen DNA language model plus a small head, then scoring facial GWAS variants. Blocked because the data cannot be found.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: no processed data located to size.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the paper's data availability statement (via library access) to see whether the multiome and spatial data are in GEO (open) or EGA (controlled); if EGA or on request, the project is dead.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: the paper is paywalled, and no open deposit of its single-cell, chromatin or spatial data was found in GEO, SRA, CELLxGENE, BioStudies or Zenodo. The only open companion record is 3 human microCT scans. Human embryonic data is often controlled-access (unconfirmed here). Revisit if the data statement points to an open GEO series.
